articleTitle: The implementation of TETRA using GNU Radio and USRP
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: TETRA (Terrestrial Trunked Radio) is a digital trunking communication standard which is recommended by ETSI (European Telecommunications Standards Institute) and has been widely used in the world. It has been used in many areas such as underground, fire protection, police system. SDR (Software Defined Radio) is a technology which just changes the software without changing the hardware to implement different communication systems. The combination of GNU Radio and USRP is such a high speed, cost effective SDR platform. GNU Radio is an open source software project which can support SDR. And USRP (Universal Software Radio Peripheral) is the hardware which is the most important hardware partner of GNU Radio. This paper focuses on using GNU Radio and USRP to implement the pi/4 DQPSK modulation and demodulation technology, the main modulation method in TETRA I. Besides, transmit and receive the modulated signal in the real wireless channel.

articleTitle: Quaternion-Capon beamformer using crossed-dipole arrays
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Adaptive beamforming using a crossed-dipole array is addressed in the hypercomplex framework. A new variant of Capon beamformer, called Quaternion-Capon (Q-Capon) beamformer, is herein proposed to fulfill the linearly constrained minimization operation in the quaternion domain. Simulation results show that the Q-Capon beamformer has a better convergence performance than the standard "long-vector" Capon beamformer, and is more robust than the latter to the uncertainty in signal's steering vector especially under the scenario of high signal to noise ratio values.

articleTitle: Wideband pulse response of monopole antenna under impact of an EMP
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A generalized mathematical procedure is developed for investigation wideband transient pulse responses of monopole antennas illuminated by an external electromagnetic pulse. The numerical algorithm is based on the time-domain integral equation solved with the method of moments. The Laguerre polynomials are implanted as the entire domain temporal basis function to expand the unknown current in the time domain. Numerical simulation are performed to capture the responses of the monopole antenna, and compared with the measured results to validate the method. The transient response characteristics of the antenna illuminated by different incident EMPs are shown and compared in detail.

articleTitle: A rapid estimation of the conductor loss in the rectangular waveguide with rough surface
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The conductor loss of the waveguide with rough surface is discussed in this paper. The surface morphology is characterized by roughness root-mean-square (rms), and the effect of roughness on the propagation properties equivalent to the conductivity of the conductor. Results for attenuation constant of S-band and Ku-band rectangular waveguide using the rapid estimation show that this method avoids the complex modeling process and greatly reduces the time to calculate the conductor losses when compared to numerical methods, thus it is more convenient for the engineering applications.

articleTitle: Ambient noise cancellation in frequency domain EMI measurement
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, an advanced signal processing technique for measurements of electromagnetic interference from electronic devices will be presented. Lower and lower ambient noise is preferred in electromagnetic interference measurement. Not all the device producers can pay for darkroom measurement, because it real costs a lot. This method provides an opportunity to perform an electromagnetic interference measurement at a site polluted by electromagnetic ambient noise. Resulted from a real device under test, automatic measurement with this method that successfully cancels the ambient noise will be presented.

articleTitle: A novel microstrip line three-way power divider
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel three-way microstrip line power divider structure using branch directional coupler is presented. The power divider is formed by two symmetrically placed branch directional couplers. The transmission characteristics of the power divider have been modeled and analyzed by using even/odd modes excitation method as well as transmission line theory. This paper also gives the design method on how to calculate the main parameters of the novel power divider. The experimental results show that this divider has excellent matching at each port and good isolation between the output ports. In addition, the structure of the divider is simple and compact and makes it easily integrated into microwave circuit system and antenna array feed system.

articleTitle: A Ka band low loss wideband E-plane waveguide filter
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents the analysis and design of a Ka band E-plane wideband bandpass waveguide filter on the basis of the equivalent circuit of the inserted strip in the middle of the waveguide broadside. According to the waveguide filter theory, the Ka band filter equivalent network parameters and its transformation are analyzed. At last, the waveguide filter is analyzed and optimized by electromagnetic simulation software. In experiment, minimum insertion loss of 0.23dB is obtained at 35.98GHz, and the insertion loss is below 0.5dB in the passband, which agree well with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Research on deeply integrated GPS/INS for autonomous train positioning
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: With the speed-up of trains, the train's positioning environment becomes increasingly complex which requires the train's positioning system have enough anti-interference capability to ensure the precision and reliability of train's positioning. GNSS/INS deeply integrated positioning system could improve the anti-interference ability of the positioning system, achieving real-time positioning with much higher precision and reliability. In this paper, a deeply integrated GNSS/INS strategy for train locating based on vector tracking loop was proposed, and the mathematical model for GNSS/INS integrated system was established.

articleTitle: Design of PLL behavioral model based on the Verilog-A
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: With the development of integrated circuits and soc (System on Chip, the system-level Chip) technology to appear, the traditional circuit-level PLL can't simulate precisely in the current EDA tools. So, this paper puts forward a method based on Verilog-A behavior-level modeling method to solve the problem. According to the mathematical model of VCO and three-order passive loop low-pass filter, establish the behavior models based on Verilog-A, pack and embed them to ADS, achieving the phase lock loop system design which composes center frequency of 120MHz VCO, cut-off frequency for 200kHz of LPF and others modules. Verify the PLL system model in ADS platform, the simulation results prove that building behavior models for analog modules based on Verilog-A not only can greatly shorten the simulation time, quickening design process, but also can effectively improve the simulation accuracy. This method has an important reference value for integrated circuit researcho

articleTitle: The broadband composite structure spiral antenna with a ladder-shaped backed-cavity
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A particular backed-cavity with a hybrid structure is proposed for a broadband composite structure spiral antenna. And the antenna is feed by an ultra wideband balun. This cavity makes the spiral antenna work operate from 400MHz to 4GHz and without the loss introduced by absorbing materials that are used conventionally to broadband spirals. Additionally, the cavity also contribute to the unidirectional radiation of microwave. Based on the reflex and superposition characteristic of microwave, a ladder liked metallic body is placed in the internal space of backed-cavity to improve the gain at the most part of the frequency range. According to the simulated results, the antenna performances are effectively improved by using this backed-cavity.

articleTitle: Adaptive bandwidth PLL design based on fuzzy logic control
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Adaptive bandwidth PLL design based on fuzzy logic control is presented for the problem of tracking poor stability and low accuracy when a certain type of radar tracking dynamic spacecraft. This method is mainly through fuzzy logic controller, adaptive level is determined by control rule of input respectively, and the outputs of rules are weighted combined to control the coefficient of loop filter, thus adjusting automatically the loop bandwidth, and enhancing the tracking stability of radar equipment and improving ranging accuracy. The simulation results show that the fuzzy logic control adaptive bandwidth PLL has higher tracking stability and accuracy.

articleTitle: A compact ring UWB antenna with tri-notch band characteristics using slots and tuning stub
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed circular ring ultra-wideband (UWB) monopole antenna with tri notched band is presented numerically. The tri-notched bands have been proposed by using two fold slots and a T-shaped tuning stub in the inner of the circular ring. The tri-notch band properties can be controlled by adjusting the length of the slots and the dimensions of the T-shaped tuning stub. The parameters of the slot and the dimensions of the stub have been investigated by using HFSS. Simulated results of the notched bands UWB antenna show that the proposed antenna with compact size of 30×22.4×1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, has an impedance bandwidth range from 2.6GHz to 10.7GHz for voltage standing-wave ratio less than 2, except tri notch band frequency 5.2GHz-5.9GHz for WLAN and HIPERLAN, and 4.0GHz-4.4GHz, 7.8GHz-8.0GHz for C-band satellite communications.

articleTitle: Make dipole antenna to be calculable over 30 MHz to 300 MHz
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A method is provided to convert dipole antennas into calculable dipole antennas (CDAs) over 30 MHz to 300 MHz. By applying a specific S-parameter adapter to a balun, the S-parameters of the balun can be measured and then the characteristics of the dipole antenna can be simulated with the aid of method of moment and the theory of microwave network. The difference of horizontally polarized site attenuation at 10 m Range between measurement and simulation is within 0.4 dB over 30 MHz to 300 MHz; the difference of site insertion loss is within 0.9dB over broadband frequencies. Application of CDA for a 5 m semi-anechoic chamber validation at vertically polarization is illustrated.

articleTitle: Dual-band meandered folded Printed Quadrifilar Helix Antenna
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a Compact Multi Strip Printed Quadrifilar Helix Antenna is presented. We use folded combining with meandered techniques to obtain 58% of size reduction for the axial length of the conventional PQHA. It creates also the dual frequency resonance. In addition, the gain remains positive at these two bands with a large beam width and a good circular polarization.

articleTitle: A miniaturized LTCC Lowpass filter with two transmission zeros
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A integrated quasi-lumped LOW pass filter (LPF) for Wireless application was designed and fabricated by low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology. The circuit is based on the quasi-lumped filter topology, and two transmission zeros were introduced to achieve sharp suppression rate. Three dimensional inductances and capacitances have been investigated and used to design the LPF. The proposed filter was designed with a cut-off frequency of 1 GHz and the measured insertion loss is less than 0.7 dB. The attenuation is less than -52 dB at 2.4 GHz and two transmission zeros are located at 2.5 GHz and 3.1 GHz respectively. The total size including the test pad is 5.6 × 3.6 × 0.9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The low temperature cofired ceramic (LTCC) materials have a dielectric constant of 5.9, a loss tangent of 0.0015, and a metallization of gold The LPF was simulated and optimized by Finite Element Method (FEM). Its good performance, small size and relatively simple structure make it a good candidate as an integrated filter to be embedded in wireless application system.

articleTitle: The influence of time delay between interference signal and reference signal to the interference cancellation system
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The interference cancellation can restrain the strong interference between high power transmitter and receiver. The main point is to make sure the time delay between interference signal and reference signal match. The paper researches on the influence of time delay to the interference cancellation system. When the interference signal is single frequency signal, the ICR is unrelated with the time delay. When the interference signal is wideband signal, the ICR is related with the time delay. The simulation analysis and experiment results explain that ICR decreases as time delay increases if the bandwidth of the interference signal is the same, and the ICR decreases as the bandwidth of the interference signal increases if the time delay is the same.

articleTitle: Analysis of electrical characteristics of LPDA and HFSS simulation design
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The electrical characteristic of LPDA is analyzed first in this paper. Simulation software HFSS is used to get the optimization design of LPDA, and the simulation results are agree with the experimental dates appropriately. This simulation method uses much less time and cost than traditional method. Therefore, this paper approves a feasible implementation for antenna design and optimization.

articleTitle: A four-way half-mode SIW power divider with improved impedance match
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A radial four-way power divider based on half-mode SIW structure is proposed in this paper. The power divider is mainly realized by a radial half-mode SIW with improved center feeding. Four microstrip lines are used as output ports. In the design of power dividers, one of the most important things is impedance match. In case for coaxial line to radial waveguide, a popular way to achieve good impedance match is to adjust the height of current probe, however, this is difficulty when facing a thin substrate. To solve this problem, we employ a ring slot besides the probe, and successfully achieve good impedance match. In this paper, we will discuss the transition between coaxial line and radial waveguide and then propose a design of a well performed power divider based on our impedance match method.

articleTitle: Noise figure measurement of multichannel phased array receiver module
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: There is a certain relationship between the system noise figure and each channel noise figure of the multi-channel phased array receiver. In this paper, theoretical derivation is proposed to find the relationship between the system noise figure and each channel noise figure based on the theory of noise figure and Y-factor measurements. Then with ADS software simulation, simulation model is built and results verify the correctness of the formula. Finally, a 9 channels phased array receiver is used to test the system noise figure and the channel noise figure. Test results demonstrate that theoretical formula corresponds to the practical relationship between system noise figure and channel noise figure.

articleTitle: A novel wide-band cascaded EBG structure with chip capacitors loading
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact wide-band electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure utilizing cascaded mushroom-like structures with and without chip capacitors loading. Direct transmission method is used to determine the band-gap of the EBG structure. The effects of loading capacitors between the neighboring metal patches on the EBG properties are investigated. The units loaded with and without capacitors are cascaded to form a wide-band EBG structure with the band widths of almost 70% The simulation and experimental results show that the overall bandgap covers the stopbands produced by the two original uniform structures. The concept of the cascaded EBG structure demonstrated here can be extended to electrically controlled wide-band structures, which would permit more optional stopbands by using electrically tuned capacitors.

articleTitle: Research on the estimation and reduction measures of antenna mode RCS of airborne phased array
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the scattering principium of airborne phased array antenna is discussed, and the antenna mode RCS of the two-dimensional array is estimated. Based on theoretical calculations, broadband matching, incline, manufacturing tolerances and other RCS reduction measures are researched. The results show that these stealth approaches have an obviously effect on the RCS reduction.

articleTitle: A 0dB crossover based on novel composite right/left handed transmission line
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a novel OdB crossover centering at 1.8GHz is proposed based on the initially proposed composite right/left handed transmission line (CRLH TL). The CRLH TL synthesized by Wunderlich-shaped dentiform capacitor and meandered-line short-circuited stub inductor (SSI) can be considered as a complete alternative to its conventional counterpart formed by interdigital capacitor and SSI. Extracted circuit parameters based on the constitutive electromagnetic parameters indicate that the left handed (LH) capacitor has increased obviously by using fractal concept. The enhanced LH capacitor is the key factor of the resultant lower resonance of CRLH cell which enables the design of an electrically smaller particle. The particular merit of the novel CRLH TL suggests potential application in compact microwave devices design. To illustrate possible application, a crossover is designed. Numerical results indicate that the crossover has received 46.2% size reduction and simultaneously exhibits comparable performance relative to its conventional counterpart.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of rectangular leaky waveguide under high speed railway environments
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The radiation characteristics of rectangular leaky waveguide with transverse slots cut in the broadside wall are studied, the effect of the high speed railway environment on the radiation property is analyzed. The equivalent magnetic current method and the method based on Love's field equivalent principle are used to simplify the calculation of radiation field of leaky waveguide. The results are in coherent agreement with those obtained by commercial software HFSS. The thickness of the waveguide has been taken into account.

articleTitle: The braking mode simulation and analysis for high-speed railway
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Braking mode of high-speed train is an important factor that affects train velocity and operation safety, the analysis of braking mode is of great significance for high-speed train's speed-up and the improvement of transport capacity. With the research into high-speed railway braking system and relative theories of the calculation analyzed, calculation of braking force, braking distance, and the target-distance mode curve, then the algorithm of braking mode curve are given in the paper, including the algorithm of the regenerative braking force, the air braking force and braking distance. In final, calculation of EMU CRH2 and CRH3 and simulation of the algorithm of braking mode are presented. The results indicate that the simulated curves keep consistent with the train braking characteristics.

articleTitle: Improved Nyquist windows for reduction of ICI in OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper proposes a new class of second order polynomial Nyquist window functions for orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system. The function is used for reducing the frequency offset induced by inter-carrier interference (ICI) at the receiver. Also, we give a method to select the window parameters to maximize the receiver SINR. The receiver with the proposed second order polynomial window is shown to have better performances of the average SINR and BER in slow fading channels, compared to the raised cosine window and "better than" Nyquist window.

articleTitle: Planar printed monopole antennas for ultra-wideband/multi-band wireless systems
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna with band rejection of WLAN/WiMAX systems and a tri-band antenna for WLAN/WiMAX applications are, respectively, proposed by the band-rejected design of the coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed circular monopole antenna. In order to notch the frequency bands covered by WLAN and WiMAX, two pieces of bent slotline are loaded at the patch bottom of the conventional UWB antenna. The proposed antenna has a good UWB characteristic with the measured notched frequency bands of 3.29-4GHz and 5.1-6GHz. In the new design of the tri-band monopole antenna, the slotline, resonant stub and radial slot are adopted to reject and control the frequency band of the conventional UWB antenna. This new tri-band monopole antenna renders the measured frequency bands of 2.25-2.8GHz, 3.3-3.8GHz and 5.1-5.9GHz for WLAN/WiMAX applications, and has a good band rejected characteristic in the other bands.

articleTitle: Design of a probe-fed microstrip antenna using differential evolution algorithm
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Design of a probe-fed microstrip antenna is accomplished using differential evolution (DE) algorithm. The fitness function for DE is obtained using cavity model analysis. Results obtained using DE are compared with those obtained by using real coded genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO).

articleTitle: Detailed analysis on combining efficiency of spatial power combining
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Spatial power combining amplifier has gained worldwide interest since 1990's and many of them have been developed in both open space and enclosed space. Combing efficiency describes the effectiveness of the combiner in summing all of the available power from active devices. Although it is one of the key figures of merit, some aspects still could not be understood clearly. In this paper spatial power combining amplifier techniques are firstly introduced. Then efficiency of such amplifiers is discussed including combining efficiency and power added efficiency. How unbalance of amplitude and phase impact on combining efficiency is analyzed in details and simulation results are given.

articleTitle: Compact broad dual-band antenna using a shorted patch with a thick air substrate for wireless body area network application
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a compact broadband antenna operated at 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz with the patch size of 22×16mm is presented. In both simulated and tested results, the desired broadside pattern, and also the bandwidth of 100MHz (4%) for 2.45 GHz and of 200MHz (3.5%) for 5.8 GHz are performed. Those bandwidths are large enough to meet the requirements of wireless body area network, respectively. The antenna gain is measured as about 0.5 dBi and 1.5 dBi for the lower and higher resonant frequency, respectively. The resonant frequency are both slightly shift down when the antenna is placed near human body.

articleTitle: Inter-cell interference coordination research for LTE
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: OFDMA has emerged as a promising physical layer technology for LTE wireless networks. OFDM solves the problem of co-channel interference in intra-cell to some extent because of the orthogonality of subcarriers, along with the character of guard interval and cyclic prefix. However, inter-cell interference still exists, especially the cell edge users suffer from interferences seriously, which leads to destroy the signal modulation of receiver. Therefore, how to improve cell edge performance to provide better QoS support has become a pressing issue. This paper focuses on inter-cell coordination, which is one of interference mitigation techniques. In other word, it gives priority to cell edge performance under the restriction of maximizing system capacity, and explores a balance between each other. Base on the perspective of radio resource management, this paper analyses coordination in terms of power control and subcarrier allocation. This paper establishes system-level simulation platform to investigate the power control scheme of soft frequency reuse and subcarrier allocation scheme. This paper proposes an optimization scheme of integrating coordination technique with MIMO beamforming. This scheme takes into consideration influence of multiple-input multiple-output gain on frequency spectrum effectiveness. Computer simulation results prove that performance of cell edge user is improved. Moreover, on the basis of channel state information of base station from mobile terminal, if capacity simulations experiment of MIMO channel introduction the application of channel state information, which prove there will be better performance.

articleTitle: A novel slotted broadband microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel slotted structure which will be etched on the patch of new microstrip patch antenna, and ground plane with crossed strip-line gaps is also used in our novel slotted patch antenna, unlike conventional microstrip patch antenna. The simulated results show that the bandwidth of slotted antenna is 13 times wider than the original microstrip antenna. Moreover, magnetic field distribution of slotted microstrip antenna is much more uniform than that of original microstrip antenna, as a result, the slotted antenna has better radiation characteristic. In addition, the 50 Ω matching is reached at the resonant frequency, therefore additional matching networks are not needed.

articleTitle: A compact broadband microstrip patch antenna for wireless router
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel microstrip printed patch antenna for wireless router in the frequency band from 2.40 to 2.483MHz is presented, fabricated and measured. Both simulated and measured results show that the return loss and the VSWR are less than -14.37dB and 1.5dB in the range of 2.40~2.50GHz, respectively. The dimension of the array antenna is 54×30mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This antenna is attractive by its simple configuration, low profile, compactness and low fabrication cost.

articleTitle: A novel broadband magic-T based on stripline-slotline transition
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel broadband magic-T based on stripline-slotline transition is proposed in this paper. The magic-T based on stripline-slotline transition has many advantages such as wide bandwidth, easy fabrication, excellent phase and amplitude balance. The working principle of the magic-T is analyzed, and the physical parameters of the magic-T with excellent performance are presented. The magic-T is simulated with a 3D FEM electromagnetic simulation software and the results are presented. The frequency bandwidth is more than 40%, when the simulated VSWR of port of the magic-T is less than 2, and the simulated amplitude imbalance is less than ±0.5dB, and the simulated phase imbalance is less than ±0.2°, and the simulated isolation between the sum port and the difference port is higher than 55dB.

articleTitle: A miniaturized, omni-directional UWB biconical antenna with band-notched
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A miniaturized, omni-directional Ultra Wideband (UWB) biconical antenna with band-notched is described Firstly, we design an antenna which is the well-known biconical antenna Then in order to improve the structure of the flat ground for miniaturization, the biconical antenna above a concavo-convex ground is designed without degrading the VSWR The antenna operates from 2.4-20 GHz with low Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR<;2). Finally, the miniaturized antenna operates from 2.4-20 GHz with low VSWR (<;2) too is designed, excluding a band-notched frequency at S.15-6GHz The propose antennas are fed by a coaxial probe through a SMA connector. The length of the proposed biconical element above the ground plane is slightly less than λ/4 at the lowest frequency in the band Simulation results for VSWR and radiation pattern of the four antennas are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Motion compensation algorithm for Airborne InSAR with severe attitude angle
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach of motion compensation for dual-antenna Airborne InSAR system with severe attitude. Phase correction which is based on baseline model is introduced to traditional dual reference track method. Experimental results with InSAR data acquired by "National West Mapping Project" airborne system shows that our algorithm can get high accuracy DEM, which testifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: DSP-based implementation of a simple space vector pulse width modulation algorithm for three-level NPC inverter
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: With the development of power semiconductor and digital processor technology, the design and application of three-level inverter in electric multiple units(EMU) are more and more extensive. The traditional space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) method for the three-level inverter requires estimating the sectors and calculating a lot of trigonometric functions. As a result, the calculation of SVPWM method for microprocessor is very complicated and large. To reduce the calculation working of the PWM module, a SVPWM method based on 60° coordinate system for three-level inverter is focused and discussed in this paper. Finally, a vector control system of asynchronous motor based on DSP was built up to verify the feasibility of this SVPWM method in this paper. Experimental results show that the adopted method can omit a lot of trigonometric functions, and reduce the calculating burden of the control system.

articleTitle: Compact dual-band bandpass filter using coupled three-line microstrip structure with open stubs
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a novel dual-band bandpass filter (DBBPF). Three open-stubs have been attached to a symmetrical coupled three-line microstrip structure. By implementing Richards' transform and Kuroda's identities, a compact DBBPF is obtained from a third-order prototype bandpass filter (BPF). A wideband DBBPF with central frequencies of 1.57-GHz (GPS) and 5.25-GHz (ISM) is designed and fabricated. The measured results agree well with the simulations.

articleTitle: Infusion monitoring system based on wireless transmission
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces an infusion monitoring system, aiming to reduce potential safety hazard of manually-controlled infusion. Dripping speed and height of the liquid level serving as monitoring signal, all data is collected by infrared as well as laser sensors. Information will then be sent to terminal monitoring interface via wireless transmission module. When the drop appears too fast or height of the liquid level gets lower than usual, the interface will give out an alert, controlling dripping speed by Step Motor automatically. The system allows a paramedic to manage the infusion process instantaneously, simply by a computer in the nurse station; it can even work automatically without a worker. To conclude, the system will economize on manpower and material resources, improving both efficiency and security. As infusion nowadays still requires much manual work, the project has a broad market prospect.

articleTitle: Miniaturized planar slow-wave antennas and their application to ultrawideband multifunction antennas
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Miniaturization of traveling-wave (TW) antennas by the slow-wave (SW) technique is shown highly promising over large instantaneous bandwidths, up to 10:1 for the unidirectional radiator and over 100:1 for the omnidirectional radiator. The technique enables a single multifunction antenna to handle virtually all terrestrial and satellite communications on an automobile, except for AM/FM radio.

articleTitle: Novel dual band-notched omni-directional UWB antenna on double substrates crossing
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel Ultra Wideband (UWB) antenna on crossed double taper-like substrates is presented in this paper. By etching L-shaped slots from the patch printed on the substrates, the proposed antenna has features of dual notched bands. Moreover, it is omnidirectional in H-plane and keeps its dominated radiating beam at about 8=45° in E-plane among the whole band. It operates from 2.6GHz to 12GHz with low Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR<;2), excluding two notch-bands of 3.65GHz and 5.5GHz with bandwidths of 600 MHz and 800 MHz respectively. The proposed antenna has been successfully simulated, fabricated and measured, showing stable gains, good VSWR characteristics and radiation performances.

articleTitle: A low voltage CMOS rail-to-rail operational amplifier based on flipped differential pairs
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces a CMOS operational amplifier with constant transconductance, suitable for operation in low voltage environments. A constant transconductance is ensured for the whole common mode input stage which is based on flipped differential pairs. The proposed operational amplifier is designed to operate with a 1-V supply and is implemented in 0.18-μm standard CMOS technology. The results show that a closed-loop unity-gain bandwidth achieves 7.6 MHz and an open-loop low-frequency gain is higher than 73 dB with a 1-MΩ||15-pF load.

articleTitle: A novel planar microstrip array antenna for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A planar microstrip array antenna applied for WLAN application is successfully designed and experimentally tested at the 5 GHz (IEEE 802.11a) WLAN band. The design was experimentally verified by constructing a microstrip array on a Teflon board and measuring its radiation characteristics at WLAN band. The measured VSWR 2:1 bandwidth in the 5GHz band is 780MHz. The maximum gain of E-plane of the proposed antenna is 19.72dBi at 5.8GHz.

articleTitle: Broadband dual-polarization dual-coverage reflectarray antenna
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A broadband dual-polarization dual-coverage reflectarray has been designed for space applications. The coverages for horizontal and vertical polarizations are 28 dBi in China and 33.5 dBi in east of China, respectively. The reflectarray consists of three stacked layers of printed arrays with rectangular patches. To overcome the frequency band limitation of the large reflectarray, the x or y dimensions of the stacked patches are optimized independently to match the required phase distribution for each coverage in a given frequency band. An approach for determining the optimal position of the feed is presented to minimize the differential spatial phase delay for the large reflectarray. The results show that the radiation patterns fulfill the coverage requirements in a 10% bandwidth (11.85-13.15 GHz).

articleTitle: Spatial power combining of active integrated antennas in microwave power transmission applications
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The solar power satellite (SPS) will serve as an important energy source in the future and many models have been investigated around the world. Microwave power transmission (MPT) is one of the most important technologies of a SPS system. A large power generation and transmission panel is often considered with emphasis in MPT research. Active integrated antenna (AIA) can be employed to construct such a panel with great advantages. Microwave power combination in open space is important to the MPT system and should be optimized. A 35GHz AIA array is presented for the demonstration experiment.

articleTitle: Implementation of digital IF receiver based on SDR using DSP builder
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A digital IF receiver is researched based on the idea of Software defined radio in this paper. The receiver includes numerical controlled oscillator(NCO), Digital Down Conversion(DDC) and the modem in a Wireless Spread Spectrum Communication system. Firstly the DDC module which include CIC (cascaded-integrator-com) and HBF(half band filter) is implemented through DSP builder, ASIC (application specific integrated circuit) design flow and verified using a FPGA (field programmable gate array) board. Then the coherent demodulation of QPSK based on COSTAS loop is researched and designed in FPGA using modern DSP technology.

articleTitle: Array beam scanning by variation of elements amplitude-only excitations
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Beam scanning in phased arrays is achieved by varying the phases of elements excitations or by frequency scanning. However, both techniques suffer from some disadvantages. It is shown here that beam scanning is also feasible by varying the magnitudes of the elements excitations thus alleviating the need for phase and/or frequency variation. Theoretical analysis and computer simulations are presented to investigate the performance of the proposed amplitude scanning technique. The performance is compared with that of the frequency scanning technique.

articleTitle: Compact dual-mode DGS resonators and its application to wide stopband bandpass filters
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel compact dual-mode defected ground structure (DGS) resonator is presented. Full-wave simulation was used to investigate the distinct characteristics of this type of resonator. The results show that it has two operating modes which don't coupled with each other and it is convenient to control the resonant frequency of two modes. Also, an inherent transmission zero could be controlled to locate at the high or low side of the two modes. A bandpass filter, using this type of resonator, has a bandwidth of 5.7% at 2.26 GHz is simulated and fabricated. The results show that this filter not only has an inherent transmission zero near the passband, but also has a very wide upper stopband with rejection better than 20 dB up to about 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Double pass-band bandpass filter using composite left-right handed transmission line
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A compact microstrip double pass-band bandpass filter utilizing composite right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission lines is designed, fabricated, and measured. Measurements are carried out using network analyzer. The bandpass filter has two centre frequencies of 7.05 GHz and 13.05 GHz, respectively. The simulated and measured results show that the proposed filter has low insertion loss in passband, compact dimensions, easy fabrication, and low cost. The novel measured performances of the bandpass filter based on CRLH are almost identical with the simulated results.

articleTitle: European train control system speed-distance mode curve analysis and simulation
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Train control system works to control the train speed, ensure traffic safety and improve the transport capacity where it is necessary to conduct systematic research on the speed-distance mode curve. The development and application of ETCS speed-distance mode curve is introduced on the basis of the ETCS fundamental principles and classifications. The classification and theory of ETCS speed-distance mode curve is focused while the algorithm and simulation of the speed-distance mode curve is briefly discussed. The model of ETCS speed-distance mode curve is core technology in the protection of foreign countries which accounts for the great significance for our study in the CTCS control curve model.

articleTitle: A composite right/left handed transmission line using fractal-shaped dentiform capacitor and meandered-line short-circuited stub inductor
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a novel composite right/left handed transmission line (CRLH TL) is proposed based on Wunderlich-shaped dentiform capacitor (WDC) and meandered-line short-circuited stub inductor (MSSI). It can be considered a complete alternative to its conventional counterpart formed by interdigital capacitor (IDC) and short-circuited stub inductor (SSI). The circuit parameters extraction and constitutive electromagnetic (EM) parameters retrieval are performed based on simulated full-wave S-parameters. These results provide a deep insight and a convincing demonstration regarding the fundamental aspects of left handed (LH) characteristic. The CRLH cell features compact due to its larger LH capacitor with respect to its previous counterpart, thus suggests potential applications in novel devices and antennas design with miniaturization requirement. The major contribution of this paper is the demonstration of the possibility of fractal geometry in the design of CRLH TL.

articleTitle: A low-profile RFID tag antenna designed for applications in UHF band
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile RFID tag antenna designed for applications in UHF band is proposed. The antenna has planar structure, and its overall size is 60 × 26 × 0.8mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It has larger inductive reactance than other tag antennas, so it's easier to match with the Philips U-CODE Gen 2 RFID chip whose input impedance is 43-J800Ω at frequency of 915MHz. Measured and simulated results of the proposed antenna are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Influence of calibration loads structure on emissivity at millimeter-wave lengths
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: By using the three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm, we investigated the optimal structure parameters of pyramidal arrays used for millimeter-wave radiometer calibration. The arrays are constructed with a periodically arranged metallic pyramids which are coated with absorbing materials. In considering the difficulties in manufacturing the sharp tips of the pyramids, we investigated the effect of two other tip shapes: flat and semi-spheric. We found that the absorbing performance of the pyramidal array with semi-spheric tips is about 10dB higher than that with flat tips.

articleTitle: Application of differential evolution algorithm to the design of a dual frequency microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new method of applying differential evolution (DE) algorithm, to design a dual frequency microstrip antenna with T-stub loading, is presented here. The fitness values of different candidate solutions of DE at each generation, is imported from the method of moment based IE3D software.

articleTitle: Load balancing routing in cognitive radio ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Cognitive radio has recently emerged as a promising technology to promote the utilization efficiency of the existing radio spectrums allocation. In cognitive radio ad hoc networks (CRAHNs), the reachability of routes depends on both network topology and spectrum availability. To adapt to this feature, a cross-layer routing protocol is proposed, which is called load balancing ad hoc on demand distance vector (LB-AODV) protocol. Previous works paid little attention to the load condition of networks, which may lead to network congestion and degrade performance thereafter. To settle this problem, we use path queue length to indicate the load condition of different paths as the primary routing metric. In addition, a hop limitation is defined to limit average transmission delay. Detailed implementation steps of routing discovery and local adjustment are described as well. Simulation results demonstrate that compared with AODV, the proposed protocol provides better performance in both throughput and average packet delivery time in CRAHNs.

articleTitle: A high gain array antenna for WLAN-WiMAX applications
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A high gain array antenna with 8×4 arrays applied for WLAN/WiMAX applications is presented. The proposed antenna is designed for the frequency band 5.07~5.94GHz with the return loss less than -15dB and the VSWR<;1.43. The largest gain of the proposed antenna achieves about 22.78dBi at 5.5GHz and the HBPW is 12.04° at E-plane. The antenna size is 285mm × 133mm. Measured and simulated results are obtained to demonstrate the promising performance required for practical uses.

articleTitle: Comparison of phase responses of proposed element shapes for reflectarray unit cells
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents design and performance analysis of various element shapes for microstrip reflectarray formed of patches of variable size. The comparison focuses on effect of the elements boundaries on the performance represented by the range and slope of the reflection phase response. Variation of the response with frequency is also investigated to assess the frequency response of the proposed elements. Various shapes in the form of patches and double-rings inspired by the Koch fractal are investigated. The analyses were performed using the CST Microwave Studio software Package.

articleTitle: Small size dual band monopole antenna for WBAN application
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a small size monopole antenna for WBAN application is presented. The proposed wearable antenna is designed for 2.45GHz and 5.8GHz. In both simulated and tested results, the band width of 200MHz (8%) centered at 2.45GHz and 1GHz (17%) centered at 5.8GHz are performed. Those bandwidths are large enough to meet the requirements of WBAN, respectively. The desired omni-directional pattern required for transmission with other wearable devices located across the body is also performed. The antenna gain is measured as about 1dBi and 4dBi for the lower and higher resonant frequency, respectively.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit of the leaky coaxial cable with rectangular slots
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents an equivalent circuit model for leaky coaxial cable with rectangular slots, the circuit model is analyzed with the help of commercial software-HFSS. The results show that the mutual coupling between slots is tiny, and can be neglected, even for the two close adjoining slots. The effect of rectangular slot parameters, such as flare angle, inclined angle, on the impedance of the circuit model is analyzed, and the corresponding radiation characteristic of the slots is then evaluated through the real part of impedance of the slot. The method of using coupling loss to compensate the transmission loss is discussed. Finally, an efficient method for calculating S-parameter of the whole LCX is given.

articleTitle: A practical suspended spiral inductor for MMIC application
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we propose an air-bridge based on-chip suspended inductor for MMIC application. The quality factor of suspended inductor on sapphire is 10.6 at 4.0 GHz, which is improved by almost 50%, comparing with traditional air-bridge based inductor of the same size. The self-resonance frequency is also improved from 9 GHz to 10 GHz. Several key fabrication processes of this suspended inductor will be presented to illustrate that our method is exactly the same as general air-bridge inductor fabrication processes in MMIC. By analyzing the equivalent circuits of RF inductors, it is shown that the suspended inductor yields lower parasitic capacitance and suffers smaller substrate loss.

articleTitle: Application of EMC design in launcher multichannel signal testing and processing system
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Aiming at the electromagnetic environments and the strict request of EMC in the field of aerospace vehicle launching, a multi-channel signal testing and processing system of launcher is setup based on several EMC design methods. The operating principles of EMC design of the system are presented, and the designing ideas of power supply, signal isolating, PCB designing and filtering are stressed on. The methods of EMC design are valuable for the design of electric devices in aerospace test.

articleTitle: High efficiency power combining of K band TWTAs for space communications
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a high efficiency power combining demonstration of two 100 W K-band TWTAs using a 4-port magic-T hybrid junction-based waveguide circuit. A low loss, amplitude and phase balanced, high power magic-T is designed for power combiner. Power combining efficiencies of greater than 90% and output power of more than 170W over a 0.6 GHz frequency band are successfully demonstrated. Such hybrid junctions can also be considered as elements within a corporate combining architecture for much higher power generating.

articleTitle: Lumped parameter modeling of transformer windings under VFTO
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Very fast transient overvoltage (VFTO) is very dangerous for the transformer which is directly connected to gas insulated substations (GIS). In order to study the voltage distribution in transformer windings under VFTO, a new model named the Piecewise Lumped Parameter (PLP) model is proposed. The piecewise lumped parameter model divides each turn of transformer windings into proper sections, whose parameters are all lumped parameters, including resistance, inductance, capacitance and conductance. The PLP model is the lumped parameter circuit model on section basis. Each section is composed of a new π-type equivalent circuit of lumped circuit model. Comparing with the results by the Multi-conductor Transmission Lines (MTL) model, this paper will summarize the reason for how to divide, that is, the relationship between the length of the section (l) and the length of wave(λ).

articleTitle: A wideband elliptic printed dipole antenna array
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An 8-element wideband printed dipole antenna array is analyzed and successfully implemented. The element used is double-sided elliptic printed dipole fed by a balanced transmission line. A wide-band balun from a microstrip feeding line to a balanced transmission line for the array was designed and implemented. Good agreement between the simulated and measured results of the array was observed. In the frequency band l-2.64GHz, the measured VSWR is below 2.0. In the frequency band 1-2.5GHz, the designed array has directional radiation pattern and its gain is between 14dB and 17.3dB. So the relative bandwidth which can meet both impedance and radiation characteristic requirements is 85.7%.

articleTitle: Novel fractal-shaped bandpass filter using quarter substrate integrated waveguide resonator (QSIWR)
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this article, quarter substrate integrated waveguide resonator (QSIWR) and fractal-shaped defected structure are used to design miniaturized SIW bandpass filters. With the QSIWR, a conventional SIW filter can be reduced in size by about 75% By using the the fractal-shaped QSIWR, the two-pole bandpass filter has simple structure, compact sizes and an extra transission zero in the upper stopband.

articleTitle: Impact of the divergence factor on accurate RCS calculation using shooting and bouncing rays
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The shooting and bouncing rays (SBR) method is a highly powerful technique for radar cross section (RCS) prediction of arbitrarily shaped targets. For the non-flat structures, the divergence factor (DF) plays an important role in accuracate RCS calculation. In practice, triangular surface mesh is widely used in computer aided design (CAD) representation for complex objects. Thus, the DF in SBR is often neglected and taken as unity. In this paper, the curvature matrices of the scattering surfaces are calculated using the surface reconstruction method. In this way, the DF can be conveniently computed by the condition of phase matching. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations are conducted to show the numeric impact and significance of the DF correction in application of the SBR technique.

articleTitle: Low-loss Z-type hexaferrite with Sr-substitution for microwave antenna miniaturization
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Magnetic and dielectric properties of conventional ceramics processed 3 Ba<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1-x)</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>O · 2 CoO · 10.4 Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (x = 0.1 ~ 0.8) hexaferrite were investigated for microwave antenna miniaturization. Sr substitution was used to modulate the high frequency properties of Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Z materials in this paper. The properties of the materials were characterized by SEM, XRD, Vector Network Analyzer, and so on. All samples showed that Z-phase was the main phase with traces of M-phases and Y-phases and the resonance frequencies were all above 2GHz. 3 Ba<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1-x)</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>O · 2 CoO · 10.4 Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> samples sintered at 1050°C had a loss tanδ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</sub> = 0.05 with the permeability of 7.5 at 1GHz and the miniaturization factor n reached a value up to 11.2 under 2GHz. It was found that Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Z samples with Sr substitution showed a better low-loss property for microwave antenna application than Sr-free samples, which was benefit for microwave antenna miniaturization and performance improvement.

articleTitle: A novel broadband low-profile array antenna with accurate beam-width for wireless communication base station
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel linear array antenna formed by the anti-phase feeding L-probe tapered patches with parasitical radiating patches and reflector ground with cutting slots is proposed and investigated experimentally. The measured impedance bandwidth determined by VSWR<;1.5 is 23.7% and it can be improved further, and the more accurate Half-Power Beam Width (HPBW) of 90+2° (the criterion is 90+8°) in azimuth plane is achieved by designing the shape of the radiation element and its reflector ground. The antenna has a front-to-back ratio of radiation pattern of 25 dB and the gain of the array antenna is enhanced by the anti-phase feeding technique. The array characters not only satisfy the wireless communication criterions but also some of them exceed the criterions, it is highly suitable for the base station applications for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Design of a low-profile compound wideband spiral antenna with embedded chip resistors
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This article presents the design and simulation of a low-profile compound spiral antenna with embedded chip resistors and a wideband balun. To obtained low-profile characteristic and solve the problem of bidirectional radiation, a lossy cavity with a horizontal balun is adopted. The simulated and measured results show that the VSWR is less than 2 and the axial ratio is less than 3 dB in the frequency range 1 to 18 GHz (18:1). In the operating band, the antenna presents good circular polarization and wideband properties.

articleTitle: Study on method for image retrieval based on feature fusion
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Single-feature-based image retrieval system of content-based video retrieval system has a lower performance. In this paper, a algorithm of image retrieval based on NMI invariable feature of dominant color and texture feature is proposed. The shape information and the spatial distribution of dominant color can be described by the NMI invariable feature of dominant color so the content feature of image can be attained easily and effectively. In order to enhance retrieval efficiency use improved gray level co-occurrence matrix(GLCM) extracted the texture feature. Combination of two types of characteristics is done. And this paper uses the method of similarity measurement for the multi-features. Experiment results show that the algorithm has a better performance.

Author Keywords: NMI invariable feature of dominant color

articleTitle: Measurement and application of magnetic induction intensity under complicated EM environment in substation
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: It is an effective method for detecting and evaluation substation's grounding grids with break and corrosion to measure magnetic induction intensity. But it will be faced with complicated EMI problem to measure effectively magnetic induction intensities in substation. So power frequency harassment and transient EMI caused by switching operations are measured practically in a few substations. These EMI characteristics are analyzed and given. The detecting system, including hardware device of data measurement, diagnosis and analysis software, was introduced concisely. The results of applications show that this system can satisfy the practical engineering.

articleTitle: Improvement on the relation between amplitude probability distribution and BER of digital communication systems
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Shortcomings of the traditional bit error rate (BER) analyzing method of digital communication systems are analyzed. Based on the amplitude probability distribution (APD) principles which are introduced in this paper, the method is improved. The error probability algorithm, which contains amplitude and phase elements of interference signals, of binary digital communication system based on APD is also introduced. It can be used for analyzing the interfering effect on digital communication systems by assuming the interference phase obeying uniform distribution.

articleTitle: Study on the data paralleled and synchronous transmission based on the virtual radio spacecraft control system
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Virtual radio space control system is the necessary tendency to spacecraft control. Spacecraft control system based on Virtual radio is different from traditional software radio in the data paralleled transmission and time synchronization. Dynamic time-division multiplexing transmission mode is presented by analyzing the data paralleled and synchronous transmission. The problem caused by traditional software radio frame that paralleled high speed data being blocked by low speed data is solved in the transmission time delay. According to uncertainty problems of data transmission and dealing time delay caused by the asynchronous work model of the virtual radio spacecraft control system, the method of time synchronization based on the data frame structure is presented, and the measure synchronization is preformed in a general way.

articleTitle: The behavior simulation of shortwave radio based on ADS
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Shortwave radio is an very important part of an aerial communication system, however it is always confronted with the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) problem when it works, so it is necessary to analyze its communication characters and the interference cases. This paper build the shortwave communication system model based on ADS, which includes the transmit and the receive part, to simulate the interference for the radio station, through which we find how the system acts when it suffers from the white noise and the narrowband interference, the simulation result is accommodated with the theory. The model can be used to analyze the EMC performance in the behavior layer, simulate the interference situation of the device, so it will be significant in the pre-design of the whole system.

articleTitle: Dual wideband open slot antenna with a band-rejected slit for 3.5/5.5GHz WiMAX and 5.2/5.8GHz WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a dual wideband open L-slot antenna with a band-rejected slit for 3.5/5.5 GHz WiMAX and 5.2/5.8 GHz WLAN applications is proposed and investigated. A slit is etched on the rectangular radiation patch to produce a notched band, which can eliminate the 4~5 GHz band effectively. Effects of varying the slit parameters on the antenna's performance show that the notched band can be finely tuned. The measured results agree reasonably with the simulated ones. According to the measured results, the proposed antenna operates at dual wideband with a fractional bandwidth of 33% from 3.06 to 4.27 GHz and anther one of 31.8% from 4.87 to 6.72 GHz, respectively. Detailed designs and experimental results are studied in this paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of composite EM scattering based on accurate geometry modeling
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An approach to studying composite EM scattering from 2-D rough surface and half-buried 3-D target is proposed in this paper, from accurate geometry modeling to RCS analysis. First, two dimensional rough surface is simulated with spectral method, which then is converted into a continuous curved surface through inverse engineering. Target model and rough surface model are combined together to be a very accurate composite CAD model, after which surface mesh is generated with the information of incidence wave frequency. Then physical optics method (PO) and multi-level fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) are respectively employed to study the scattering problem. The results of single rough surface and combinative model are given and the results by the two different methods are compared.

articleTitle: Prediction formula for flat-roofed effect in near-field scattering of conductor flat
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The aim of this study is to establish the quantitative expression about flat-roofed width in near-field scattering of conductor flat. At the basement of phenomenon analysis, we have made a theory derivation of the flat-roofed width function of some parameters, such as distance, size and etc. In addition, the precision of predicted results have been verified by physical optics method. From the expression and its results, it can be seen that the prediction formula is desirable in analyzing near-field scattering of the flaggy targets.

articleTitle: Genetic algorithm in suppression of quantization side-lobes of phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Phase quantization errors appear in phased array antenna utilizing the digital phase shifter for beam steering. And this cause relatively high parasitic side-lobes. This paper demonstrates the application of genetic algorithm (GA) in reducing the phased quantization errors effects on parasitic side-lobe level of phased array antenna. GA has the ability to escape from local minima and maxima and is ideally suited for problems where the number of variables is very high. The results of simulations, accomplished using the methods of random phase feeding and GA are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: UWB fractal monopoles of rectangular and triangular shapes
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Fractal concept has been used for broadbanding printed monopole antennas to comply with UWB requirements. The concept of self similarity has been deployed, where repeated square and triangular shapes form the composite monopoles to increase their frequency ranges. In each of the designed antennas, the shape has been scaled up then repeated in vertical direction away from ground plane. The proposed monopoles showed enhanced response at both lower and higher frequencies to cover more than the entire UWB band. The performance of the proposed monopoles were investigated by simulation using the CST computer software. The phase of the return loss has been used to explain the behavior of the proposed monopoles.

articleTitle: Simulation of shielding effectiveness test with bounded-wave EMP simulator
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The shielding effectiveness (SE) test is usually implemented in the bounded-wave simulator. However, numerical simulating the SE of a shielding enclosure is mostly modeled with plane wave incidence. In this paper we present the parallel FDTD method to analyze the SE of a shielding enclosure in bounded-wave simulator. An improved formalism for thin slot is adopted. The result shows that the result obtained in the simulator is higher than the plane wave simulating result. From the numerical results, we can find the law of the results between bounded-wave simulator model and the plane wave model.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic interference on localizer beam using in parallel runway
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Under the conditions of the parallel-runway at airports, the impact of the electromagnetic interference caused by an Airbus_A320 with the fuselage parallel to the runway and the tail toward localizer antenna on the localizer beam of the ILS (Instrument Landing System) is analyzed in this paper. Firstly, the model of the electromagnetic environment of the localizer is established, including the localizer antenna and its associated transmitter, the numerical aircraft scattering model, and the receiver and subsequent data processing. And then the simulated data are calculated by means of the computer. Finally, according to the simulated data, the parameters impacting much on the multipath interference will be found and the solution will be advised to reduce this interference. And it will be much useful to find out the optimized routes of the operating aircrafts with the help of the data.

articleTitle: Transformation optics collimating lenses for multi-beam antenna applications
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Transformation optics (TO) is a flexible design process for electromagnetic and optical devices with a wide range of applications including cloaking, waveguides, and antenna enhancement. Many TO designs for antennas have been proposed, such as invisibility-cloaking radomes and collimating lenses; however, these designs all require inhomogeneous and anisotropic material parameters with extreme values that do not promote a practical implementation. Thus, the choice of transformation is a critical part of the TO design process and determines whether the device can ultimately be fabricated. In this paper, we review two transformation designs with simple material parameters for the conversion of radiation from an embedded isotropic source into multiple highly-directive radiating beams.

articleTitle: Multicarrier modulation techniques for TETRA II
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: TETRA is a digital trunked communication system. TETRA II adopt Filtered Multitone Modulation (FMT) multicarrier scheme to provide high speed data service. This paper introduce modulation parameters which are defined in TETRA II standard and efficient implement, then simulate and analyze the BER performance in AWGN and multipath channel.

articleTitle: Analysis on the phenomenon of line harmonic content amplification for AC-Driven Electrical Multiple Unit
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In the type test process of a certain type AC-Driven Electrical Multiple Unit (EMU), because of the logical error of pulse rectifier's carrier phase shifting control, line side harmonic content is amplified. Transient value of line voltage increases and the normal work of other EMU under the same power supply arm is impacted. Through harmonic analysis on test data and line side harmonic characteristic of EMU, this article finds out the reason why line harmonic content is amplified. By modifying pulse rectifier's control software, successfully solve the problem of too much line side harmonic content in the operation of the EMU.

articleTitle: An approach for the design of Cylindrical Surrounding Double-Gate MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we have explored the designing approach of Cylindrical Surrounding Double-Gate (CSDG) MOSFETs, for the wireless telecommunication systems to operate at the microwave frequency regime of the spectrum. This proposed CSDG MOSFET can be used as the RF switch for selecting the data streams from antennas for both the transmitting and receiving processes. We emphasize on the basics of the circuit elements as drain current, resistances at switch ON condition, capacitances, energy stored required for the integrated circuit of the radio frequency sub-system. Using this device we analyzed that the drain current is higher, ON-resistance is lower which shows that the isolation is better in CSDG MOSFET as compared to single-gate MOSFET and double-gate MOSFET.

articleTitle: The design of ferrite film phase shifter
publicationTitle: 2011 4th IEEE International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces the basic operation principle, structural characteristics and microstrip impedance-matching network of ferrite film phase shifter.
